sources.title: Beijing Bird's Nest Stadium & Water Cube Complete Guide
sources.content:
Beijing Bird's Nest Stadium & Water Cube: Complete Guide

Bird's Nest Stadium (Beijing National Stadium)

History & Construction
The stadium was designed by Herzog & de Meuron, Arup Sport, and China Architecture Design and Research Group. "Construction started in 2003 and finished in 2008, just in time for the Beijing Olympics." It holds 91,000 people and represents the world's largest steel structure.

Design Features
"The stadium gets its name from the interlocking steel elements that resemble a bird's nest, a design choice meant to symbolize a cradle holding the hopes of the world." The interlocking design enables natural ventilation and sustainability.

Visitor Hours
- November 1 - March 15: 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM
- March 16 - October 31: 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM

Ticket Pricing
Adults: 100 RMB; Discounted tickets: 80 RMB. Children, seniors, and people with disabilities may receive free entry or special discounts.

Interior Access
Visitors can access the first, second, and fifth floors. The fifth floor offers the best photography opportunities and includes a Skywalk observation platform with sweeping views of Olympic Park and Beijing's skyline.

Transportation
Take Beijing Subway Line 8 to Olympic Park Station or Olympic Sports Center Station. Multiple bus routes (82, 419, 538) also serve the area.

Water Cube (National Aquatics Center)

Architecture
Designed by PTW Architects with China State Construction Engineering Corporation and Arup, "its design, inspired by the natural formation of soap bubbles, is both visually stunning and highly functional." The exterior consists of over 3,000 ETFE pillows providing superior insulation.

Purpose & Features
The facility hosted swimming, diving, and synchronized swimming during the 2008 Olympics. Post-Olympics, it transformed into "Happy Magic Water Park," Asia's largest and most technologically advanced indoor water park.

Activities
Visitors enjoy waterslides, wave pools, play areas, and the popular Bulletbowl and Tornado rides. Public swimming sessions allow visitors to experience Olympic pools where world records were set.

Practical Information

Getting There
Both venues sit in Olympic Green, easily accessible via Subway Line 8. "Both the Bird's Nest Stadium and the Water Cube are within walking distance" from Olympic Sports Center Station.

Recommended Duration
Allocate at least half a day to experience both venues fully.

Nearby Attractions
- Olympic Forest Park (680 hectares with lake, trails, observation tower)
- Olympic Green Convention Center
- China National Convention Center
- Multiple shopping and dining options

sources.title: Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest) 2026: Visitor Guide, Tickets & Highlights
sources.content:
Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest) - Complete Content Extract

Overview
The Beijing National Stadium, commonly called the "Bird's Nest," is an iconic architectural landmark that hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and 2022 Winter Olympics ceremonies, making it the only stadium worldwide to host both summer and winter Olympic opening/closing ceremonies.

Key Facts

Location & Hours:
- Address: 1 National Stadium South Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing
- Hours: 10:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily (last entry 9:00 PM)
- Night lighting: Approximately 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM

Physical Specifications:
The stadium covers "204,000 square meters of land, with a construction area of 258,000 square meters" and holds 80,000 permanent seats plus 11,000 temporary seats. Construction cost was 2.267 billion RMB.

Architecture:
Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron designed the structure to resemble a bird's nest, symbolizing life nurturing and humanity's aspirations. The design combines "cutting-edge engineering and aesthetic brilliance."

Visitor Information

Tickets:
- Standard panoramic ticket: 100 RMB (adults); 80 RMB (seniors/children)
- Combination ticket (Bird's Nest + Water Cube): 138 RMB (adults); 108 RMB (seniors/children)
- Free admission: Children under 6 years; seniors 65+

Recommended Visit Duration: 2-3 hours

Main Attractions:
1. Golden Hall - Features "double Olympics" exhibits, Olympic torches, and mascots Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
2. Grand Stand - VIP viewing area with panoramic stadium views
3. Xiangyun Gold Hall & Liushui Silver Hall - Elegant reception halls with traditional Chinese design elements
4. Steel Forest - Fifth-floor architectural showcase featuring intricate steel framework
5. Skywalk Tour - 1,000-meter rooftop walking route offering views of the Water Cube and Beijing skyline

Transportation

From Downtown Beijing:
- Subway Line 8 to Olympic Park Station (B1 Gate), then 10-minute walk
- Bus 419 or 538 to National Stadium East Station
- Taxi: approximately 40 RMB daytime, 30 minutes travel time

From Beijing Capital International Airport:
- Airport Express + Subway: ~60 minutes, 30-35 RMB total
- Taxi: 80-100 RMB, 40 minutes
- Airport shuttle bus: ~90 minutes, 27 RMB

Dining Options
Shuang Ao Food Street near the Water Cube specializes in Beijing snacks, including "Old Beijing Pear Soup" and "Egg Puff Ice Cream."

Accessibility
The venue is "stroller-friendly" with "spacious interiors and well-designed pathways" suitable for families with young children.

sources.title: Beijing National Stadium - Features and Travel Tips
sources.content:
Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest) - Complete Information

Overview
"Beijing National Stadium is located at the south section of Beijing Olympic Park, and was the main stadium of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games." The venue has become a popular tourist destination due to its architectural significance.

Key Architectural Features

Structure: The stadium features a deliberately complex, multi-layered design with no apparent geometric pattern. The construction incorporates multiple converging levels throughout.

Environmental Design: "The design of the Bird's Nest fully reflects the concerns of sustainable development." It employs advanced environmental technology, natural ventilation, and lighting systems.

Viewing Experience: "The ingenious design ensures the distance of the line of sight from every seat to the center point is about 140 meters." The venue accommodates over 200 wheelchairs and provides hearing aids and broadcast systems.

Appearance: The structure resembles a massive bird's nest and can hold 100,000 people. Designers included Jacques Herzog, artist Ai Weiwei, and CADG.

Visitor Information

Specifications:
- Area: 21 hectares
- Height: 69 meters
- Seated capacity: 91,000
- Service life: 100 years

Access Details:
- Admission: 50 yuan (stadium only); 80 yuan (with Water Cube)
- Hours: 9am-7pm (April-October); 9am-5:30pm (November-March)
- Duration: approximately 1 hour
- Location: Olympic Park, North Fourth Ring Road, Chaoyang District

Transportation: Multiple bus routes available; Subway Line 8 serves the location.

sources.title: How to visit Bird's Nest and Water Cube
sources.content:
Complete Guide: Visiting Bird's Nest and Water Cube

Overview
The Bird's Nest (Beijing National Stadium) and Water Cube (Beijing National Aquatics Centre) are iconic structures from the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games that continue to attract international visitors seeking to experience these architectural landmarks.

Transportation Tips

Subway Access (Recommended):
"Take Subway Line 10 and get off at Beitucheng Station. Then interchange for Subway Line 8 and get off at the next station to the north - Olympic Sports Center"

The Olympic Park itself is free to enter. Alternative bus options include routes 409, 426, 645, 653, 656, 658, 660, 689, 694, 740, 753, 758, 803, 839, 849, 850, and 858.

Taxi travel is discouraged due to parking difficulties.

Visiting Recommendations

Evening vs. Daytime:
Evening visits offer superior visual experiences. The Water Cube displays changing color patterns each evening, while the Bird's Nest features illumination from solar panels that collect energy during daylight hours, creating a magical nighttime appearance.

Interior Exploration:
Visitors can choose between exterior photography only or exploring interior structures. Time availability and personal interests should guide this decision.

Practical Information

Operating Hours & Fees:
- Bird's Nest: 09:00-18:00, 50 RMB entry
- Water Cube: 30 RMB entry
- Water Park (additional): 200 RMB
- Swimming only: 50 RMB

Visitor Volume:
Approximately 20,000-30,000 daily visitors frequent the Olympic Park, with roughly 5,000 entering the Bird's Nest or Water Cube daily.

Best Times to Visit:
Avoid weekends and public holidays when crowds are heaviest and ticket availability is limited.

Future Developments

The facilities are evolving into comprehensive leisure centers. A high-end Olympic Theme Restaurant operates in the Bird's Nest. Winter plans include converting the structure into a ski resort for seasonal festivals.

sources.title: Beijing Bird's Nest (National Stadium): Architecture & Facts
sources.content:
Beijing Bird's Nest (National Stadium): Architecture & Facts

The Bird's Nest is a stadium at Olympic Green in Chaoyang, Beijing, China. Designed by Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron, the stadium's groundbreaking architecture was inspired by Chinese ceramics and features a latticework exterior that mimics a bird's nest. It hosted the opening and closing ceremonies for the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics.

The stadium covers an area of 204,000 square meters with an 80,000 person capacity. Entrance fee is 50 RMB, allowing you to visit the interior of the National Stadium which is densely packed with nearly 100,000 red spectator stands.

The Bird's Nest has become home to the winter's Happy Ice and Snow Season gala, featuring a 100-meter-high ski slope with tons of artificial snow, and a magic blanket is set on the east side to take you up to the top of the slope.

After the Olympics, the stadium transitioned into a multi-purpose venue and today is a vibrant hub for entertainment and sports, regularly hosting major concerts, sporting events, and cultural performances.

Best Time to Visit: Many visitors recommend seeing it illuminated at night for a breathtaking spectacle. Night lighting: Lights are turned on around 8:00 PM and off at 10:00 PM.

Getting There: Line 8: Get off at the Olympic Park Station. Exit B1 or B2 will lead you directly to the stadium. Routes 82, 538: Drop you right in front of the stadium.

sources.title: National Stadium, Bird's Nest - My Beijing China
sources.content:
National Stadium, Bird's Nest

The Beijing National Stadium, also known as the Bird's Nest, is an architectural masterpiece located in Olympic Green Village, Chaoyang District. The stadium covers an area of 204,000 square meters with an 80,000 person capacity.

The design implemented steel beams to hide supports for the retractable roof, giving the stadium the appearance of a bird's nest, and leading Chinese artist Ai Weiwei was the artistic consultant on the project.

Entrance to the interior allows you to see the densely packed nearly 100,000 red spectator stands. A walk around the stadium is also worthwhile, especially in the evening when it is beautifully lit.

The Golden Hall on the ground floor features the "Double Olympics" exhibition area with artifacts such as the Olympic torch and mascots. The Skywalk Tour on the rooftop provides a panoramic view of the Olympic Park, including the Water Cube and Beijing's iconic central axis.

The Bird's Nest Stadium and Water Cube are within walking distance of each other, making it convenient to visit both on the same day.

Ticket Pricing:
- Basic entrance fee: 50 RMB
- Sky Corridor tickets: 80 RMB (elevator to the top on the north side of the fifth floor)
- VIP tickets: 110 RMB (includes VIP area with golden hall and lounge)

Walking around the exterior is free and offers great photo opportunities.

sources.title: 国家体育场_百度百科
sources.content:
国家体育场（鸟巢）完整信息汇总

基本概况

国家体育场，又名"鸟巢"（Bird's Nest），位于北京市朝阳区北京奥林匹克公园中心区南部。该建筑是2008年北京奥运会主场馆，也是2022年北京冬奥会和冬残奥会开闭幕式场馆，成为全球首个"双奥开闭幕式场馆"。

建筑规模

- 占地面积：20.4公顷
- 建筑面积：25.8万平方米
- 观众容纳：9.1万人
- 建筑尺寸：南北长333米、东西宽296米、最高处高69米
- 竣工时间：2008年6月28日
- 总造价：22.67亿元

设计与建造

建筑由瑞士建筑师雅克·赫尔佐格和皮埃尔·德梅隆领衔，联合中国建筑设计研究院共同完成。中方总设计师为李兴钢，负责方案本土化及技术实现。

建筑结构特色

鸟巢的外形结构由24根巨大的门式钢架组成。建筑采用"结构即立面"的设计理念，将钢桁架围绕碗状坐席区编制成椭圆形。主要特点包括：

- 钢结构用量：4.2万吨
- 设计使用年限：100年
- 抗震设防：8度
- 屋顶覆盖：双层膜结构（透明ETFE膜和半透明PTFE声学吊顶）

功能布局

基座以上共7层，设有观众服务设施、媒体工作区、贵宾接待区和商业区。基座以下共3层，包含零层内部环路、停车场和功能用房。碗型看台分为上、中、下三层，上中层间设有140个包厢。

重要活动记录

体育赛事：承办2008北京奥运会、2022北京冬奥会开闭幕式、意大利超级杯足球赛、2017英雄联盟全球总决赛等。

文艺演出：自2009年成龙演唱会开始，已举办逾400场文体活动，包括歌剧《图兰朵》、《中国好声音》鸟巢巅峰之夜等大型文艺活动。

演唱会：五月天、张杰、华晨宇、林俊杰等众多知名艺人在此举办个人演唱会。

文化意义与运营

作为国家形象的标志性建筑，国家体育场已成为国际交往平台。2014年获评"中国当代十大建筑"之一。

参观信息：
- 开放时间：10:00-22:00
- 门票价格：成人票100元/人，优惠票80元/人

运营成果（截至2026年2月）：累计接待中外游客和观众超1200万人次，举办文体活动400余场次。

sources.title: 北京鸟巢(国家体育场)游玩攻略 - 携程攻略
sources.content:
鸟巢(国家体育场)游玩攻略

基本信息
鸟巢（国家体育场）位于北京市朝阳区国家体育场南路1号，营业时间为10:00-22:00（21:00停止入园）。

门票价格
- 鸟巢普通门票：50元/人
- 鸟巢和水立方两馆联票：80元/人
- 鸟巢、水立方、中央电视塔及国家大剧院套票：190元/人
- 80元的鸟巢空中走廊票可以乘电梯上到顶部，透过脚下的钢网眼能看到纵横的钢结构和内景观
- 110元的贵宾票除了包含参观票和空中走廊外，还增加贵宾区、金色大厅等设施

冰雪季活动
2026年北京第十五届鸟巢欢乐冰雪季营业时间为2025年12月27日至2026年2月下旬，位置在朝阳区国家体育场北路1号院鸟巢，早鸟票为58元/人，工作日门票120元/人、周末及节假日160元/人。

游玩建议
鸟巢内部有近10万个红色观众席，同时展有鸟巢建筑工程和奥运主题相关展览。到了夜晚，鸟巢亮起红色的灯，旁边水立方蓝色为主的灯光相映成趣，在人工河边可以拍摄鸟巢与在水面的倒影。

交通
地铁8号线奥林匹克公园站B1口出，步行约10分钟。
